title: Fire Emblem Fates Was Sold as Two Games, Like Pokemon
hook:
Fire Emblem Fates launched in 2015 as two separate cartridges, Birthright and Conquest, with a third path sold as DLC and a 500-page script from a manga writer. It became the fastest-selling Fire Emblem launch the US had seen. Which path did you pick first?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Fire Emblem once sold its story as two separate games, the way Pokemon does? Fire Emblem Fates launched in Japan in June 2015 as two retail versions, Birthright and Conquest. Each one shared the same opening chapters, then split onto a different side of a war. Birthright was built for newcomers, with maps you could replay to grind experience and gold. Conquest removed that safety net, so every battle counted. Once you owned one version, the other path could be bought as a download for twenty dollars. A third path called Revelation arrived later as downloadable content, and a special edition put all three stories on a single cartridge. The script came from manga writer Shin Kibayashi, who was asked for about ten pages per route and turned in roughly five hundred. The gamble worked. In the United States the game sold more than three hundred thousand copies in its first three days, over five times what Awakening managed. By early 2017 Nintendo's figures put it at about 1.6 million copies worldwide. One thing did not survive the trip west. Nintendo cut a touch screen mini game where you petted characters' faces from the English version. Would you buy a game split in two like this again? Follow for more gaming history.
